cornerCallouts: They're through the start/finish straight, now braking hard for turn 1, a critical overtaking opportunity on this 1961 layout.
Now, into the esses! Maintaining momentum through this section is key to a fast lap.
The cars navigate the gentle right-hander of turn 3, setting themselves up for the long back straight.
The long back straight allows the drivers to really open up the throttle. Top speeds will be reached here before braking for the bus stop.

strategyPoints: Tire degradation will be a major factor on this 3.701km layout. Managing the rubber is crucial for a strong finish.
With the shorter lap length, pit stops will be critical. A quick stop can gain valuable track position.
Fuel consumption will be tight. Teams will need to carefully monitor their fuel levels throughout the race.
The relatively short lap means more opportunities for safety cars. Teams need to be ready to react quickly.
The pit window is likely to be quite wide, giving teams some flexibility in their strategy. However, traffic could play a significant role.
Overcut or undercut? That's the question teams will be asking themselves. Track position is king here at Watkins Glen.
The historic layout is very demanding on brakes. Teams will need to ensure their cars have adequate cooling.
The balance between straight-line speed and cornering grip is crucial. Teams will need to find the optimal setup for this unique circuit.
weatherCommentary: The weather in upstate New York can be unpredictable. Sunshine one minute, rain the next!

The wind can also play a significant role, especially on the long back straight.
The hills surrounding the circuit can create microclimates. Different parts of the track may experience different conditions.
The humidity can be quite high here at Watkins Glen, which can impact tire performance.
